attempts.raw_response: He emphasized that the government’s hesitation was causing unnecessary suffering for families across the country. The opposition leader called for immediate clarity on school closures to allow parents to plan and protect their children. Without decisive leadership, he warned, the healthcare system would remain under unsustainable pressure. Sir Keir argued that delaying action only prolonged the uncertainty and economic damage. He urged ministers to prioritize public safety over political optics, stating that swift intervention was the only way to restore confidence. The situation demanded urgency, not further debate or delay in implementing critical measures to curb the spread of the virus effectively.

In March last year, Boris Johnson told people in England they could only leave home to exercise once a day, travel to and from work when it is "absolutely necessary", shop for essential items and fulfil any medical or care needs. Currently, shops selling non-essential goods have been told to shut and gatherings in public of more than two people who do not live together are prohibited in tier four areas. Sir Keir said the government's message needed to be firmer and backed by law, if necessary, to encourage people to comply.
